notes.title: The Community Update (1.2) - Dev Diary
notes.content:
Hey everyone!! The next big update for Carnaval Simulator is almost here: The Community Update (1.2). This update is packed with new features, improvements, and fun additions to enhance the game's possibilities. As always, we value the input from our amazing community, so keep those suggestions coming on Discord! Now, let’s dive into the exciting features coming your way in this update.

Enhanced Visitor Interactions
1 of the biggest most exciting new features is the enhanced visitor interactions. Visitors can now engage in small talk, discuss the location, comment on the music, and even complain about the weather. They can also give compliments or criticize your float, talk about construction clubs, power outages, and much more. These dynamic conversations bring the parade to life and make the game more engaging than ever before.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/27bf249ca86d745e7401bd8e4624abd93aa85294.png

Barrier Feature
When a lot of visitors come to watch your parade, barriers will automatically appear to manage the crowd. This feature adds to the realism and helps control the flow of spectators.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/0db0a286d0fcd2f5a0ccd4c01ec0a733faa7ff3e.png

Standalone Tractors
Introducing the Standalone Tractor! Now, you can have your tractor float without needing to attach other carts. This gives you more flexibility and creativity in your parade designs. Experiment with different setups and see what works best for your vision.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/2bf0f1b687daa45d806cf09af2db50cd9d301253.png

To help you get started with the new Standalone Tractor feature, we’ve added a dedicated campaign level. This level will guide you through all the possibilities and nuances of using a standalone tractor, making sure you get the most out of this new feature.

Additionally, we’ve introduced a possible new trait for your floats: the Frontal Cart AI Preference. This trait gives more points for well-decorated tractors, encouraging you to put more effort into making the front of your float as impressive as possible.

Pop Up System
Our new Pop Up System will keep you on your toes with random fun news, warnings, and alerts. These pop-ups add an extra layer of excitement and unpredictability to the game, making each playthrough unique.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/04aa98a50231ce7085639dad2245ad86cb1804c2.png

Better UI
We’ve revamped the main menu UI to include better descriptions and visuals of the location map. Now it’s easier than ever to navigate and understand the various options and settings available to you. Similarly, the campaign level menu has received a UI upgrade. Enhanced descriptions and a more intuitive layout ensure that you can jump into the action without any confusion. As well as an improved building menu UI for shadows, more items, slimmer and overall intuitive.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/d9e412bdb0a212dd9166edc578cc88056dce6710.png

Unique Polyester Graphics
This will make your floats look more smooth and visually appealing, adding to the overall immersion of the game.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/c2c86e5113e4646a136022b30f4f1a8d5caaa98f.png

New Camera Scene: Rotation
We’ve added a fancy new camera rotation feature! This allows you to rotate the camera around your float, providing you with stunning new angles and perspectives.

And much more!!
The full update log will be released when the update goes live, detailing all the new features, changes, and fixes. Development is ongoing, and we’re also working on blueprints, grouping, pulling tractors, adjusting cart lengths, decoratable generator cart, props for even more creative possibilities and much more! Expect this update to roll out in the coming weeks, and stay tuned for more updates!

Thank you for your continued support and enthusiasm. Let’s make Carnaval Simulator the best it can be!

notes.title: The Grand Expansion Update (1.1) - Dev Diary
notes.content:
Hey everyone!! The biggest update Carnaval Simulator has yet received is still work in progress: The Grand Expansion Update (1.1). This update will contain new content and a bunch of bug fixes (especially rotations making them user-friendly). The update includes an overall massive improvement of the game hence its name. All updates for Carnaval Simulator are heavily influenced by the community's wants and needs and are combined with the vision I have for the game. So if you have any wishes or suggestions, make sure to let us know on Discord! Without further ado, let's show what's to come in the upcoming update!

Fountain Fireworks
Just like in real life, some floats both at day time and at night use fountain fireworks to impress its audience. The upcoming update will include 2 types of fountain fireworks: regular & large. The large one can only be placed once per float. These are high-level items, akin to other show elements such as smoke machines.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/de82c31d12c40b7bcbe83f859d878a7f5d239f23.png

Colorable lasers
While adding new content is really fun, sometimes it's also crucial to return and update some of the existing items. The option to change the colors of lasers has been added, enhancing customization options for lights. More customizations for lights are in the planning stages.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/888116ab73c84eac421521ea35fa688fdb2fb602.png

New Smoke
Speaking of smoke, smoke effects have received a massive graphical update, enhancing realism and interaction with colorful lights. In real-life, I love seeing the smoke being used in combination with colorful lights so of course I had to find a way to make this possible. It's far more realistic overal including the way it floats around.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/badf441bf8e8abcf11d7df80a1a917ee0dbc4d0b.png

Old smoke:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/d88307b20e09506d72826a9b74277086c4943b91.png

Letters & Numbers
A very much requested feature is the ability to add letters to your float. All the letters of the latin alphabet have been added. Now you can spell things out or use them in a very creative manner. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/0febc7daec22e1f56e898fcb80afedb0c0dead20.png
And of course, when I added the letters, why not add the numbers?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/d30a6441f9d5d9867413ab12e3b5361a0a58e5e3.png

Confetti
Players can now throw confetti for added interaction in first-person mode, providing an enjoyable and fun addition to gameplay. This fun little gimmick ended up to be way more enjoyable to play with than I expected. And yes, you can spam click to throw a lot of confetti.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/ed69992b4596c2a8e5fff0e855abb6e5e86f0dfa.png

New flags
Additional flags representing major German Carnival cities will be included in the update.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/a187fe55d0884fb2ea6dbbde3f130c3dc4cb800f.png

Water
Water has been added to Farmlands. Not a major feature, but I love how it turned out visually. I don't wanna say too much about the future, but let's say it's gonna be reused in some way or another ;)
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/363ed6c7b89639358968b9412bda4d062e515168.png

And much more!!
The full update log will be released as soon as the update hits, featuring numerous additions, changes, and fixes. Currently, developement is focussed on the long promised customizable front cart as well as a revamped score system. Additionally, more characters and other props are being worked on for further creative possibilities. When will this update hit? It will take a few weeks to finalize the update. It is expected to be released around Easter, but it may arrive later in April. I will keep you guys up to date! 

Lastly, all promised features mentioned in the last anouncement are still on the table, except for the durability mechanic. We have bigger plans for this one in the next Disco & Weather Update (1.2).

I have made my general plans for the year all the way up to Carnaval 2025 for the game's official release. Great things are ahead of us, this will raise the game's quality massively. 

So what will be in this major update? Well I already made a post about the plans for Carnaval Simulator a while ago. Plans have changed in some ways though due to revisions, community feedback or it got added to the game already. 
 
Here's what to expect:

 Customizable front cart (finally hidding your tractor)
 Proper stretch mechanic -> stretch your props in certain ways

 Durability mechanic, affected by the temperature
 A better value system for each prop
 Crew progression perks -> crew becomes more useful
 Honking in multiplayer
 Throwing confetti in first person
 More loading screens
 More camera controls
 More props -> currently I can promise a new character, the rest is a secret


Besides these new features, I will always try to fix bugs whenever I can. I am really grateful to all people reporting these bugs. They all get looked at.

Old promises that have been altered:

 Spectator camera -> already added in update
 Rearrangement of the mod structure -> moved to the future
 More modable options -> moved to the future
 Better learning curve / more balanced game -> already dealt with but changes may still occur all through out development


I will keep you guys up to date on the progress. I cannot provide an exact release date but this information will follow. Smaller additions like a button to enable all rotations in build mode may be added too but I will let you guys know about this as the update progresses. notes.title: Dev Diary 21th of Jan
notes.content:
Greetings folks! Welcome to the fourth and last pre-release dev diary of Carnaval Simulator. This dev diary is a bit late due to the game blowing up last week. It's a very exciting and stressing time. Right now we are very busy fixing all bugs and tweaking the last things. We are potentially adding more props & finishing touches here and there. Preparing for the release on friday around 11:11. The full game will cost 10,99€/10,99$ including free updates.

Anyway, now that's out of the way, we will be focusing on the contents of this dev diary. We are gonna reveal new details on multiple carts, polyester, lights, light patterns, synced lights, mix lights & light shows in this one.

Multiple Carts
An obvious addition to the game is the ability to add an extra cart for more building space. Of course, when you boot up the game for the first time you cannot purchase an additional cart yet. First you will have to play around a bit and level up in order to unlock the ability to add an extra cart. Pulling the float takes quite some weight and resources so usually this is not worth it unless you have maxed out the first cart already. Adding an extra cart will provide you with some additional points, although the resources it takes is mostly greater than it is worth unless the aforementioned scenario is taking place. 

When adding a new cart it will appear somewhere around the construction site. The weight limit is universal however the balance mechanic is separate for each cart. It will update the UI once you start building or altering a specific cart.

Moreover, you know what's even better than 2 carts? 3 carts. So making the longest parade float is possible in Carnaval Simulator. However the third cart is unlocked when you are a very high level. It's basically a very late game upgrade. I may wanna make this an unlockable once you completed all campaigns or a certain scenario level but that's still up to change. 

Lastly, it's also possible to add a generator cart behind all your other carts. For now you cannot alter it, however there will be an update allowing you to customize it with props granting you even more points with interesting mechanics. Do note that the customizable tractor cart will be introduced earlier than this one. More about this in the next dev diary
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/f40668248048e51a87feaa79ee7a427adc46b8b8.png

Polyester
When you reach higher levels in Carnaval Simulator the game unlocks more and more features. One of these features is the polyester upgrade.

In real life, parade floats can be made from all kinds of materials. Mainly materials such as: paper mache, styrofoam, paverpol and polyester. In Carnaval Simulator, the props are made out of paper mache normally. However, you can turn them into polyester. Just like in real life, you may wanna add a layer of polyester on the existing props to increase its durability. Polyester is incredibly durable material (although chemical) compared to paper mache hence paper mache floats usually don't last various years and are prone to damage during harsher weather conditions. Above all, you may also create more detailed shapes compared to paper mache. 

I thought it would be an interesting game mechanic to upgrade specific pieces with a bit of strategy. Of course, this is only valid during single player. This mechanic is prone to change as we MAY add weather conditions in the future. For now, there's no durability mechanic YET. However, upgrading your pieces to polyester possibly grants you with extra points due to the more detailed shapes (fictionally). To avoid this mechanic from becoming very tedious and unmanageable, I came up with an interesting twist: you may gain more points from the same prop. Basically repeating the same prop over and over again will eventually grant you with less and less points for each piece. By upgrading some of these pieces you gain special 'material/polyester' points along side your normal score. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/2e98c2d5ae624d0463f891dcd52c6114d7070889.png

Lights & Light Patterns
An incredibly important game mechanic in Carnaval Simulator is being able to add lights and modify them. During a night time parade this is an absolute must in order to gain any points. During the day time this will only grant you with a very small amount of points making it a total worthless decision.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/2f297d7ecb761d2466b5393eddc8e8d6aea87731.png

In Carnaval Simulator, there are various lights to pick from. All have slightly different values making them play differently. All of them require electricity and you will need to purchase in-game DMX Console for your float. Once you have bought the console, you may alter the lights from the UI.

So what can you alter? The most important feature are the light patterns. You may select 1 specifically but you can also have a randomized one or an ordered one. You may create your own playlist/sequence of light patterns this way. See the image below for reference.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/65b2869a9c6a90719da65343b0e27b43e824d02d.png

You may alter the speed of the pattern but also the transition time. During a transition, it dims the light until it becomes fully on or off (depending on the circumstances). Setting it to 0 will result in an instant turn on and off. It's basically a fade in & out.

Available light patterns on release:

 Off
 On
 Standby: lights are dimmed
 Music: deprecated but still usable light pattern based on your music
 Flicker: turns lights on and off
 Wave per light group
 Wave per light group reversed
 Wave per cart
 Wave per cart reversed
 Fall: vertical wave per light group
 Rise: reverse of the above
 Train: turns each light group on, off, on, off etc. in such an order
 Train reversed: reverse of the above
 Appearing: very randomly on and off based on light groups

Most light patterns utilize light groups. In Carnaval Simulator, lights are usually assigned automatically to their light group. You may also manually adjust this or merge different groups. See the image below for reference. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/acccdc97a8138f5012b1c2755ee1b91c5212ec23.png

As you can see there are many more options. The game contains tooltips for almost everything to help the player. Here are a few of them explained:
The light intensity is how bright all lights will be, minimum light intensity is the lowest brightness lights can have. 
Static pattern speed is the timespan for each pattern. 
Pattern rotation speed is the time it takes to reach the next pattern. 
Beats per pattern is the amount of beats it takes to reach the next pattern (music feature).
Transition speed is the timespan for each transition.
Height factor is the distance factor to be activated during a fall/rise pattern. 

Usually you do not need to alter these values. Hence they are hidden in the advanced options.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/020080f96c257f77f464215e53a5c7224b49767a.png

Last but not least, there's the option to enable the speed based on the music of your float. This will be talked about in the next chapter.

Synced Lights
All it takes to sync the lights to the music is clicking the toggle button mentioned before. This will essentially force the lights to listen to the beats of the selected song. The most important setting is the tedency to recognize these beats. You can press 2 buttons: the snail & the horse. This will automatically generate a value that fits the music. Of course, this option isn't 100% accurate for every song in existence but it does a great job. It really depends on the song that is uploaded. Otherwise, you may alter the value yourself. A lower number means a lower tolerance so basically you are likely to get more beats recognized in your song.

Time steps are optional but can be handy. They define how many beats can be recognized within a specific timespan. Increasing the value will delay recognizing each beat.

Moreover, there's the hard beat bias. Hard beats are different from normal beats. They are more rare thus harder to get. They can be enabled and disabled if the player wishes. This feature will try to alter light patterns once activated. For example, when a song starts to get super loud/more intense suddenly for that extra epicness. Lastly, the 'ticks for pause moment' option works very similarly except it activates when there's no music being played for a certain amount of time. Lowering this value causes this feature to activate during shorter times of silence during the music if there are any. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/1890c17d79f4ab30b42fbaacc4b513b99c3af531.png

Mix Lights & More Light Options
Our next light related topic: mix lights. This feature can be activated in spotlights. You essentially can mix 2 different colors. There's a value for the transition speed and a value for how long it takes to activate the next transition. They are really awesome, they can be combined with light ropes for a really awesome view.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/156262822e714ca22fc8dec1216b28e71dd2c4e6.png

As you may have noticed, there's also the option to ignore the light pattern. Every buildable light has this option. This way you can just ignore the light pattern settings and have it turned on for ever. Enabling this option also reveals the possibility to enable a timer so you can activate the light for a certain amount of time. You can alter the delay and its duration. Lastly, there's the option for hard beats to dictate the light's activation for that extra epicness like mentioned before.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/cb4bc18fcf61f16c5f8e9243a354ebfd9b2d30f0.png

Light Shows
Huh? But didn't we cover light shows already with regards to the light patterns? Perhaps in a way.
However, I wanted to introduce an even more advanced light show system to take it to the next level. You will need an ECS Console. This allows you to create your very own light show based on a specific action and assign a light group of all light groups to it. You can enter the start value and end value. They are calculated in seconds. There's also the additional speed value. The show also needs a show to be selected. This will be your show song which is different from your normal one.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/d2109f2962d3313172d23c8fbea1defc0b552658.png

During a parade you may activate the show and gain extra points. However it may exceed the amount of power you need risking a power outrage. You gain more and more points for each show you activate during the parade. It's a risk-reward situation. 

However, as the game develops in early access, I would like to improve the user friendliness of the UI as there's currently no way to really listen back to the music and set each sequence to the right second. It's not the most important feature of the game so I will flesh it out in a future update. For now, the light show feature is disabled in multiplayer for this very reason but it will become available at a later point. Above all, I feel like the current light pattern system is advanced enough for the average player.

Final Words
Wow, that was a lottt of information. I believe I have covered most of the features of the game. I wonder what you guys think so please leave any suggestions in the comments. Next dev diary will be a short one. I will give a quick rundown on the upcoming plans and features for update 1.1.0 (the first major update) & beyond. It's gonna contain a lot of new information, so stay tuned. Ciao!!

notes.title: Dev diary 11th of Jan
notes.content:
Greetings folks! Welcome to the third dev diary of Carnaval Simulator. Last time I mentioned that we will be talking about further details on perk mechanics, different game modes, slewing rings (rotations), music and the balance mechanics. Last time I also mentioned the light shows but I have decided to move them to the last dev diary for next week due to the amount of features related to the light mechanics of the game. So let's get started with the said topics.

Perks
To add more strategy to the gameplay of Carnaval Simulator I wanted to create the possibility of having perks that you can choose each game that gives you a specific benefit. This can really make a difference in case you are in need of something specific. For example you have some energy left but you need more weight because you built too many props on your float. You look at the goal information and you see the parade is in daylight. In this situation lights aren't important so you can sacrifice your energy limit for a lighter generator. Or you are really wanting a specific character at one side of the float, well you can enable the perk bonus to create a better balance on the float. There will probably be some clutch perks but I think the less powerful ones are situational. I like that qua game design because balance doesn't always define the fun factor.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/aa1971bf95537e2fb3262191144c6e1e7fe8fd47.png

Initially the perks could be chosen again after each day so they would reset. After some testing I figured it would be way more fun to choose a new perk each day but also keep the old ones so it really feels like you are upgrading your float in a way. I love upgrading things in games and getting stronger, better, more organized etc. I believe this makes the game more enjoyable. This is also what I tried to incorperate into the game with the leveling system; you start simple but as you progress your floats can become more and more impressive, beautiful, bigger and more complex. This is what the perk system represents on a smaller scale. 

I wanna add more systems like these in future updates in which you can upgrade your float in a tycoon sense. Stay tuned for future dev diaries on this one

Game Modes
To make the game extra interesting, Carnaval Simulator contains various game modes:

 Scenario/campaign mode
 Multiplayer mode
 Challenge mode
 Custom mode
 Sandbox mode
 Parade mode

We have already been talking about the scenario mode & multiplayer in former dev diaries. Hence I will skips these and I will be talking about the other 4. 

Challenge Mode
This mode is unlocked in late game, at the moment by getting to a high level but it might become an unlockable mode after completing all the scenario plays. It's meant to provide the player with a refreshing challenge after completing all scenarios. In this mode, you play for 99 days and every day provides you with a new challenge to complete because after each day, the seed refreshes. The seed determines all kinds of values such as the theme, motto, prize money temperature etc. these affect the gameplay thus creating some randomly generated challenges. As days go by, your time becomes a bigger and bigger limitation so it becomes progressively harder. 

In the future, I wanna add more randomness & challenge to this mode by integrating some of the unique features in the scenario play (such as colorless props, starting without cash etc.). 

Custom Mode
In this mode, you create your very own scenario level simply by editing the values of the game. Very similar to a custom scenario from the workshop except this is user friendly due to the presence of an actual UI instead of editing a script. You cannot gain any experience from this mode.

Sandbox Mode
As the name suggests, it's a mode in which you can just play around with unlimited money, weight, balance etc. You cannot gain any experience from this mode either but it's simply fun to play the game without any constraints whatsoever.

Parade Mode
Personally I think this is the most interesting mode. In this mode you get to assamble an entire parade by using the floats you have made before. You can simply drag and drop them around to adjust the position. In total, you can have a parade of up to 8 floats. In the near future I wanna increase this limit.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/065167ff9e4a768f1cfc48ee4e36453cb4f7222d.png
Note: the UI of the main menu is still work in progress

Slewing Rings
In order to create a more dynamic float you should add slewing rings to your float. In real life, these slewing rings are used to rotate certain parts mechanically such as a character's head, a wheel or another kind of prop. In Carnaval Simulator, they provide you with extra engagement points since you create a more dynamic experience.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/40ff5ae23442dae4caa3cc0e81ed67a1c7e5a241.jpg

I have been pondering how to make a user friendly UI for these rotations. I came up with a having buttons that allow you to drag the rotation in a starting position and an ending position. There are also buttons to make it spin in a certain direction. Last but not least, you may alter the values manually. You can adjust the speed as well, making it negative means you reverse the rotation into the opposite direction.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/38d68cfddf8071590f8606b6cad1e61ec7946f55.png

EDIT: you can also link different props to your prop's rotation from the object window, eliminating the need to purchase a new slewing ring for each one. You can even add a slewing ring on these linked props for multiple rotations. For example, you may want a blade or another item to rotate, and simultaneously have smaller props rotate vertically with the blade – all of which is possible. Of course, you can also unlink them if needed. It's worth noting that while most props support slewing rings, some, like devices, do not.

Music
Music is an important part of the game. In real life, floats often use mechanical music nowadays to add to their atmosphere of the creation. In Carnaval Simulator, you should add music boxes as well as an amplifier to add the music to your float. There are currently 2 music boxes for the sake of strategy differing from stats (price vs weight vs power). The amplifier is used to be able to set and adjust the music. Adding music to your float is important for your score. Adding way too many music boxes may grant you penalties to your score. Make sure to divide them well over your carts so every part is covered with music otherwise you may lose points.

Above all, music can be uploaded from a folder. Any music may work. This allows the player to enhance the creation with fitting music. As you can see, there are also advanced settings but they will be further explained in the next dev diary about the lights. There's basically an entire beat system that you can alter so it recognizes how many beats the music should generate for the lights.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/008d2d43c954e0d4673ae482514379a724ad50b8.png
Balance
To make the game a bit more challenging I added the balance mechanics. Another major reason why this mechanic is important is so that it encourages players to build a more symmetrical float which overall looks so much better. Of course, you may add a different character on the other side of the float. As long as they are the same weight it won't affect you. The current system is very tolerant so you can add plenty of things on one side without any downsides. It's only to punish the players who really go out of their way. However there's a perk to help with the balance so if you really wanted to do something else for some creative reason you still can. In sandbox mode, this mechanic is disabled.  

Final Words
That was it for today! The next dev diary will be the last one containing the last details for the current game; multiple carts, polyester, lights & light shows. The dev diaries that shall follow will be about the future and upcoming updates. The next dev diary will be published next week, so stay tuned. Ciao!!

notes.title: Happy New Year!! Dev Diary 3rd of Jan
notes.content:
Greetings folks! Welcome to the second dev diary of Carnaval Simulator. As promised in the last dev diary, I will be revealing more details on the parade float designs (and its backlog), multiplayer, drive mechanics, tractors and more so let's get started.

Parade Float Designs
Most props the user can build from the build menu are themed ones. These themed props are based on pieces of existing parade floats for the sake of authenticity. For Carnaval Simulator, I have requested permission from IRL parade float building organizations (which are all volunteers doing this as a major hobby almost all year round). Most of these organizations gladly wanted to contribute to the game and will therefore be listed in the credits of the game as a form of honor. Some of the props are based on parade floats as old as the early 2000s. So this game is a way to digitally preserve these parade floats into the digital age. I think that's beautiful.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/7392f6c118d5715957b330b7581099461a377974.png
In-game buildable character is made from 3 kinds of props.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/de1a6b6989d17322c36fcca3272d4936565d6137.jpg
The IRL version of the above mentioned character on a real life float. 

Of the many parade float designs I have received, I have picked a handful to begin with. I prefer the ones with a distinct theme which works well with the theming mechanic of the game. First I begin with dividing the parade float up in pieces and deciding what should be digitally modelled and what can be left behind. Sometimes it gets tricky due to the artistic nature of certain pieces which makes it hard to divide into proper props within the game. 

As of now, there are 3 parade floats digitized. Another one is work in progress which brings the number to 4 for release. This might become 5 but it depends on how far I will get. This number might not seem much but for every float, it adds many new props that the user can combine. The way the user creates the parade floats reflects how some IRL organizations operate: buying pieces, recoloring them and reassembling the float itself. Whereas moddellers (who provide models to the Steam Workshop mods) reflect the organizations that create these floats from scratch. 

The parade floats in the backlog will remain a secret. Like I have done in the past, I drop some hints first for each parade float I introduce to the game. I will continue doing so for future updates through out 2024. I may also go back to some floats I have made so far and polish them up or add some brand new props for the details that I have left out in the past (such as a smaller less significant character). But for now let's give you guys a little sneak peak what's to come:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/b5576a29a12c11f64fae75d27517a2f81c71ee92.jpg
Beach themed parade float design made by BC de Bokkerijders. This one will appear in the future updates.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/9d22ebb7fca6f85773b12a331ae38acab5987a19.jpg
The IRL version of the above mentioned float.

Multiplayer
In my vision of the game, this is perhaps the most important part of it. The multiplayer gameplay brings a lot more replayability in the game. It works similar to singleplayer but there are still some distinct differences. The most important being: the score system. When a player creates a match, others may join the game up to 8 players. Everyone will create their own parade float and once everyone is done or you all have run out of time, the parade scene begins. Each player will be able to bring out a vote for each parade float that drives by. It's entirely possible to have a set theme before beginning or a certain motto which we will later talk about. 

Players are able critique each other's creative skills in this way which is far more interesting than the AI deciding the score based on a large number of factors. This is what happens IRL as well. A select few people govern over the scores the parade floats receive. The more players join, the more interesting the outcome becomes. For now the limit is 8 players but I may increase this with an update. I will have to experiment with how much the game can handle and create more performance options for the player so players with slow computers may play the game as well despite the large number of floats (especially very big ones). For now, 8 players is enough. I imagine you may not able to always find 8 players. In this scenario, the players can enable the AI to give out the scores without the voting system. All the settings can be determined by the host of the game before beginning. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/8f46e26b69eedf19479512572c6eb1b4b5948f94.png

Last but not least, multiplayer is a great way to gain a solid amount of 'experience' to level up. If the player has played all campaign levels, the multiplayer mode becomes the most optimal way to play the game and level up.

Drive Mechanics
A highly requested feature is being able to drive your very own parade float. This was a tough one with regards to game design. The way it works within Carnaval Simulator is that the player (or the host) sets the speed of the parade by using the buttons in the menu. They may also pause the float entirely which means the rest of the floats also stop. This essentially makes the speed buttons universal over the entire float. But another way to control the speed is to really drive the float itself. It's more like a novelty than an important game mechanic. The way it works is that you enter a tractor and you can drive forwards & backwards. The steering is completely automatic within the parade and the rest of the floats within the parade drive on your speed to avoid colliding with each other. 

Game design wise it would get very tricky to have manual steering for 2 main reasons:

 Multiplayer; users don't wanna wait forever just for some person to finish driving
 Driving along colliders can easily cause physics issues when it comes to the carts behind you (especially with 3 of them)

However this does not mean that there will be no future update that adds the ability to drive around more freely. Do not count on it but I won't say no to the possibility. Who knows, maybe some of you have some great suggestions on how to properly handle these scenarios so make sure to share your suggestions in our Discord server! However, at the in-game construction sites of the parade floats, players may take a free ride around the site with their tractor which they can steer freely.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/a328551c1146f1c495f0df2d489613c43097521a.png

Tractors
Tractors are an important part of the game as they pull the parade float itself. In real life, tractors are very common to pull these floats. Sometimes other vehicles are used but it's usually a tractor. In Carnaval Simulator players are able to upgrade. Upgrading means they improve the tractor so it can pull more weight therefore increasing its weight limit so you can build an even bigger float for a higher score. Additionally you may also recolor the tractor for a small bonus score. If the color of the tractor matches the rest of your parade float (there's an entire color check mechanic) you gain the bonus points.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/6a5ef9a0ea9a5b6f57a05859508b09b54990a0fa.png

Most importantly, in the upcoming version 1.1.0 (after release) there's gonna be a possibility to turn this tractor into a buildable front cart just like what happens often IRL. This will be an additional way to gain points. The above mentioned beach float shows this as well. There's the main cart and the front cart. This would really enhance the gameplay of the game I believe. Hence I didn't dedicate time making different tractor models for each upgrade. After version 1.1.0, the player will usually have to make their own front cart to gain more points so unless you just start out, this will become an absolute must to win. 

Themes, Traits & Mottos
In the last dev diary we have touched upon the goal description but underneath there are some very important details. The most notable ones are themes, traits and mottos. Themes define the theme you should build your float in. They provide you with a lot more points which is absolutely required to win. Building an impressive float outside its theme will heavily disadvantage you. You may still win but as you play along, the campaign levels get harder and harder so eventually you won't be able to cheese it. The trait is a specific aspect which grant you extra points. Not very important but it can help you just a bit more to gain victory for the golden cup.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/a6fc959923b2208d15b3c0c16954881e34e9c1d7.png

Lastly, mottos are usually funny phrases or short puns by itself. These are entirely cosmetic but may play a key part in multiplayer. There are 2 types of mottos: the default motto and the user-made motto. The idea is that users alter the motto in a way that it expands on it just like in the real life celebration. This adds an extra layer of creativity to win the votes of other players. The default motto is set by the world seed or the host. The user may alter it for their float which will be shown when viewed during the parade scene. 

An example would be: "Rolling the dice" for the default motto: "On a roll". But you could take this even further, who knows you make a music themed float and call it: "let’s rock and roll". Or you could make something about literally rolling. You could get very creative and use it in all kinds of ways to make others smile or just for the sake of novelty.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/845f0b06204abd5e350cc47a4f02fcc802af0e8d.png
Motto for a pirate themed parade float.

Release Date & Price
The release date of Carnaval Simulator is now official: 26th of January. The game will receive free updates after its release. The price will be 10,99€. The use of other currencies may affect the price. 

Final Words
That was it for today! There are more topics to cover in the next dev diary which will provide further details on perk mechanics, different gamemodes, slewing rings (rotations), music, balance mechanic and light shows. This upcoming dev diary will be published later in January so I will see you guys then. Ciao!!

notes.title: Merry Christmas!! Dev Diary & Roadmap to Release Jan 2024
notes.content:
Greetings folks! First of all, the development of Carnaval Simulator is still on-going. I have been seeing huge progress which is key to its release in January 2024. Due to the size of this dev diary I will be splitting this up in different parts (next dev diary in early January). Let's share this dev diary and reveal the roadmap for 2024, so what are my plans for the future? What is already finished? How's the development going? This is gonna be a long one so let's get started!

Build Maps
Let's start with build maps. Within Carnaval Simulator, you create your parade float on your building terrain. This is a separate map from the city. In real life, these parade floats are typically made in rural and industrial areas. Therefore I have tried to make various maps distinctly different from each other yet sharing this common real life fact. At release there will be 3 different maps: Denlake Valley (a forest map), Farmlands and Industrial Area. These maps are unlocked when you level up. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/ab048e27ba01997195ff24a5967af79961392f8f.png

It's mostly cosmetic for the sake of immersion except for the resource locations scattered around the map. Resources are mostly given at the start of each game or rewarded by winning parades but a small bonus can be found within the map itself. Additionally one may also find collectables around all maps. They aren't visible in the camera mode so they are harder to spot! Finding them rewards you with fun facts about the real life Carnival celebration. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/e3246723eb6430e08d3117cac735aebdb5d6353a.png

City Map
As mentioned before, there's a separate map for the city in which the actual parade takes place in. Also in this map you will be able to find collectables. In singleplayer this is mostly the visual presentation of your float and you will get your results at the end. In multiplayer this scene lets the players vote for each float that comes around. For release, it's my goal to fully finish the map with all its important details. In the future I wanna add more maps for more variety. They will be parodies of real life towns which are meaningful to the real life celebration and who knows, we may travel around the world? Lastly, the amount of build maps (3) are currently efficient for the end product, but they may receive small visual updates in the future

Campaign Levels
An important gamemode in Carnaval Simulator is the campaign mode (singleplayer). These are all unique levels that provide the player with unique challenges. Examples of these levels are: being very tight on time so you will have to create your float very rapidly, all props being built without color which teaches you how to color the props (they give you extra points for doing so), specific themes giving you the points necessary to win, starting without any resources but you will have to find them scattered around the map in first person mode and much more! They essentially help you teach the game further. There's a tutorial in game which teaches you the very basics but this will help you understand the mechanics more deeply. I think it's way more fun to learn from these challenges. Above all, they give you special EXP when you complete a level as well as unlocking the next level. 

For release I will be tweaking the existing campaign levels and create some new ones as new mechanics are being developed (such as the limited stock mechanic). 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/4d67dd646ab2fe7aacca6188dda26e21a1d597d9.png
Note: main menu UI is still WIP

Each time you complete a level you will see its cup spinning around. All you need to do is becoming third for the bronze cup for you to unlock the other levels. For the completionists, you will have to try to gain gold on any level. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/10a3a2dc0d7a45cebf49c9948f2153682c7e9ab5.png

Steam Workshop
Mod support is crucial to extending the lifespan of games like Carnaval Simulator for creating more unique creations and engaging challenges. Therefore, I have decided to prioritize mod support so users can upload and download custom content very easily. Right now users may share custom props, custom music and custom campaign levels. After downloading them you will only have to open the game to see the custom content appear. This will further extend the possibilities to user's creations.

Additionally, there's an option to share your own creations as you can see in the workshop. Your very own floats can be shared, similar how you may share a world or map in other games. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/e8e8f30a8d48ae21b963c09d49ea71f7c7d5ee89.png

The way you create these mods can be examined through the examples on the Steam Workshop. But I may add a simple guide on Carnaval Simulator's website as well. Right now the only limitation is that you can't make 1 main mod that adds music, props etc. all together. You will have to create separate mods for this. After its release I will restructure the mod system so you will be able to create everything in 1 mod and perhaps more customization options as the features of this game will grow. I am curious what people will create!

Score System
When playing single player or with very few players you may let the AI decide which float gains the most votes. There are various categories to gain points from:

 Float rating
 Excitement rating
 Height rating
 Music rating
 Light rating
 Bonus rating

Right now the player will be able to view how well they did in a specific category so they can reflect and construct an even more impressive float! A very difficult aspect to this was the balance between creative freedom vs interesting gameplay mechanics. I have tried to provide the player with as much creative freedom as possible within certain constraints. Each campaign level additionally offers different challenges but also non-campaign modes generate specific traits & themes that provide the player with additional points based on the world's seed. This system will receive constant updates as the game develops so expect changes in future updates! I will not go deeper into how these points are granted since it is ultimately the jury's decision.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/9e8dfe8b88e317afeb0efb483b59c3e43a232ed9.png

Crew Mechanics & Limited Stocks
A very much requested feature for this game is the ability to add crew members. I essentially turned the citizens from the town map into crew members and added mechanics around them. I created limited stocks for certain items and integrated this with the staff members as well. The size of your float determines how many you assign to your crew. They aren't necessary however but they do help you with your excitement rating which is given for the interactions between your float and the crowd. 

They have the same simplistic look as the citizens in the city for the sake of consistency. This is intentional so we can add lots of citizens for better performance. In the future, I may update the graphical look of them but for now it's not a priority. They perform random dances, and their outfits are also randomly generated (although you can customize them)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/739ebba743dffab3eea4cc099d22b1b1a62b3503.png

In the future I would like to expand on this mechanic for more depth to the game. Expect more options to interact with your crew in future updates! 

Achievements
For now there are 11 achievements in the game. This perfectly matches another system I have built which keeps track of various statistics based on your gameplay, such as the number of props you have placed or the amount of floats you have built. In the future we may add more achievements but that's low priority for now. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44737934/9114f6529539538d36908f42309a4956c5aa8b9d.png

Release date & Price
Carnaval Simulator will be released sometime between mid to late January. The game will receive free updates after its release. The exact date of release will be revealed very soon as I am finalizing the details! Last but not least, the price will be 10,99€. The usage of other currencies may alter the price. 

Final Words
That concludes 2023 for us. The year has been filled with extensive development of Carnaval Simulator. Make sure to join our Discord server to follow the development of Carnaval Simulator, all suggestions are welcome. Hope you all have a great Christmas and a happy new year. We look forward to returning in January for the next dev diary where we will talk about parade float designs (and its backlog), multiplayer, drive mechanics, tractors and more, see you then!
